newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Ruling party split colours elections in Montenegro.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party split colours elections in Montenegro.

text.p: Momir Bulatovic and Milo Djukanovic, heading rival factions in Montenegro's ruling party, will run against each other in the Yugoslav republic's presidential elections in October.

Political tensions were bound to increase after the Montenegro Electoral Commission cleared republican President Bulatovic to take on Prime Minister Djukanovic although they are both in the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS).

One DPS faction, headed by Djukanovic, engineered Bulatovic's removal last month from the post of DPS president, accusing him of taking orders from Serbia, the other, more populous and powerful republic in federal Yugoslavia.
Bulatovic is believed to be close to Slobodan Milosevic, the strongman former president of Serbia who has just taken over as federal president.

The Djukanovic group feels that the reluctance of socialist, authoritarian Serbia to undertake democratic and free-market reforms is penalising reform-minded Montenegro by prolonging Yugoslavia's international isolation.
Bulatovic's faction accuses its foes under Djukanovic of plotting secession from Yugoslavia.
Bulatovic loyalists held their own party congress last week insisting on keeping the DPS name and assets and decided to nominate Bulatovic as their presidential candidate.
Djukanovic, however, has been confirmed as DPS candidate too.
"The majority (RIK) members had the view that citizens should decide among the candidates and that both party wings should have the same election chances," a senior political source told Reuters.
But the decision violated republican law which allows a party to have only one candidate for elections.
"The DPS is not a single party any more. It is split into two separate parties," the same source said.
If any of the candidates appeals against the decision, the constitutional court would have to rule within 24 hours.
